scope: Static weight-algebra extraction of the direction a published rank-1 abliteration removed. Two safetensors files are read in float32; dW = twin - base per writeback tensor; SVD per tensor. No model is loaded, no forward pass, no generation, no GPU, no benchmark. Removal is NOT measured here: every claim below is about weights, and a behavioural claim would need a served model (out of scope).
caveat: The twin is stored as bf16, so dW = bf16(base - edit) - base carries a rounding floor. Untouched tensors are not all-zero; they are classified by relative delta norm and reported separately.

weight_algebra.method: dW = W_twin - W_base [out, in]; u1,v1 = top singular vectors, sign fixed so the largest |u1| entry is positive and v1 flipped with u1; shared axis = top right singular vector of the (2*n_layers, hidden) stack of u1; strength_ls_shared_axis is the least-squares a in dW ~= -a r (W^T r)^T with r = shared axis; residual_frac_shared_axis_rank1 = ||dW + a r (W^T r)^T|| / ||dW||.

lm_head.weight.note: lm_head exists only in the twin (the base file is tied and has none), so it is compared against the base embedding it was untied from

repo_diff_beside_weights.note: weights are the only thing this experiment reads; the twin repo also ships its own chat template and pad token, so any behavioural comparison against it would carry that confound as well as the weight edit

checks.rank1_note: rank1_share_sv = s1/sum(s), which is diluted by the 896-long singular-value spectrum and is NOT a rank-1 measure; rank1_energy_share = s1^2/sum(s^2) is the rank-1 measure; sv2_over_sv1 is the bf16 rounding floor

run.note: BLAS must be single-threaded here: scipy-openblas spawns 64 threads on 32 cores and an SVD of 896x4864 goes from 1.7 s to over 60 s.
